assumptions.A01: Fixed local Eulerian tetrad with signature (-+++), x0=c t, homogeneous fixed-volume source substep. Photon lab energies and directions stay fixed in this substep; geometry and spatial transport retain their separate ownership.
assumptions.A02: One common gas velocity with |beta|<1; D=gamma n_H>0 and f=n_He/n_H>0 conserved. Physical H/He fractions, neutral-reference mass constant, r=m_ref c^2+epsilon_eV B>0, rho=n_H(r+epsilon_eV w), p=(2/3)n_H epsilon_eV w, Gamma=5/3. Bound-electron rest masses are already included in m_ref.
assumptions.A03: Finite directional photon nodes have nonnegative lab number densities and nonnegative prescribed lab sources. Node spectral/angular weights are already included. Individual beam directions have unit spatial norm.
assumptions.A04: Retained FT03 Case A CI/RR/two DR/primary absorption and captured kinetic moments; CR/RCT/HH off. Rest T in [30000,110000] K, gas-frame photon energy in [0,50000] eV. Fit cutoffs (13.60,24.59,54.42) eV and binding energies (13.598434599702,24.587389011,54.41776) eV keep distinct roles.
assumptions.A05: All rate, fraction, density, electron closure, temperature and Doppler inputs share one candidate endpoint. Proper event density R' per proper volume and time produces lab event increment h R' per fixed lab volume. Per-H species changes divide by D; the equivalent proper-clock step is h/gamma.
assumptions.A06: Case A escape is a comoving-isotropic emission-moment closure with inherited RR/DR binding plus captured-kinetic power Q'_esc. Its lab energy and scaled momentum increments are h gamma Q'_esc and h gamma Q'_esc beta.
assumptions.A07: The local full-source theorem uses a strict composition/primitive/warm/active-photon-energy interior and C1 rate/source dependence in a neighborhood away from fit cutoffs. A quantitative contraction bound additionally uses a fixed scaled norm and a closed convex ball in that smooth physical domain.
assumptions.A08: Full directional nodes support arbitrary velocity. Existing azimuth-averaged rings reduce exactly to a one-dimensional adapter for axial velocity; transverse velocity uses a positive resolved azimuth quadrature or the corresponding pointwise angular integral.
